{

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Client-side upload size limit is hardcoded to 10MB",
      "body": "validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the limit depended on whether the upload was an image or attachment and on the admin-configured site setting. It now always allows 10MB. This can let users select attachments larger than the configured attachment limit, and can also block images when the configured image limit is larger than 10MB."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js",
      "line": 246,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit",
      "body": "displayErrorForUpload now tells the user that the maximum upload size is 10MB after a 413 response, regardless of the actual site setting or web server limit. This can display an incorrect maximum size to the user."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 55,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "URL downloads ignore configured upload size limits",
      "body": "FileHelper.download was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes for all URL-based API uploads. This ignores both max_image_size_kb and any attachment size limit, allowing the server to download up to 10MB even when the configured limit is lower."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "In-place downsizing can corrupt or destroy the uploaded tempfile",
      "body": "The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) and ignores the return value. If the conversion or optimization fails, truncates the file, or produces a corrupt image, the original uploaded data has already been overwritten and the controller may continue to Upload.create_for with a damaged or zero-byte file. A separate output file and explicit failure handling are needed."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Animated GIF downsizing is invoked with an invalid percentage geometry",
      "body": "The controller passes dimensions='80%' to OptimizedImage.downsize. For animated GIFs, OptimizedImage uses gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}, and gifsicle expects WIDTHxHEIGHT rather than a percentage. The command will fail, so large animated GIFs will not be downsized and the loop will either retry uselessly or proceed with an oversized file."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 64,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Automatic downsizing is attempted for vector images such as SVG",
      "body": "The condition uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which treats SVG as an image elsewhere in Discourse. OptimizedImage.downsize is a raster ImageMagick resize and cannot meaningfully or safely reduce an SVG file in place. Large SVG uploads will repeatedly fail downsizing or may be corrupted before upload; vector formats should be excluded or handled separately."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/optimized_image.rb",
      "line": 149,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Duplicate downsize method definition breaks the previous four-argument API",
      "body": "Ruby keeps only the last definition of self.downsize, so the new three-argument method at line 149 silently replaces the four-argument version at line 145. Existing callers using downsize(from, to, width, height) will now have height interpreted as opts, or will raise ArgumentError if an options hash is also supplied. This is an API break and can cause TypeErrors or invalid resize dimensions."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
      "line": 64,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior",
      "body": "There are no tests for the new server-side downsizing loop, including oversized images, failed conversions, animated GIFs, SVGs, or interaction with configured size limits. These cases are likely to regress and are risky areas of this change."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Client-side upload size limit is hardcoded to 10MB
findings.body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the limit depended on whether the upload was an image or attachment and on the admin-configured site setting. It now always allows 10MB. This can let users select attachments larger than the configured attachment limit, and can also block images when the configured image limit is larger than 10MB.

findings.title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit
findings.body: displayErrorForUpload now tells the user that the maximum upload size is 10MB after a 413 response, regardless of the actual site setting or web server limit. This can display an incorrect maximum size to the user.

findings.title: URL downloads ignore configured upload size limits
findings.body: FileHelper.download was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to a fixed 10.megabytes for all URL-based API uploads. This ignores both max_image_size_kb and any attachment size limit, allowing the server to download up to 10MB even when the configured limit is lower.

findings.title: In-place downsizing can corrupt or destroy the uploaded tempfile
findings.body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) and ignores the return value. If the conversion or optimization fails, truncates the file, or produces a corrupt image, the original uploaded data has already been overwritten and the controller may continue to Upload.create_for with a damaged or zero-byte file. A separate output file and explicit failure handling are needed.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing is invoked with an invalid percentage geometry
findings.body: The controller passes dimensions='80%' to OptimizedImage.downsize. For animated GIFs, OptimizedImage uses gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}, and gifsicle expects WIDTHxHEIGHT rather than a percentage. The command will fail, so large animated GIFs will not be downsized and the loop will either retry uselessly or proceed with an oversized file.

findings.title: Automatic downsizing is attempted for vector images such as SVG
findings.body: The condition uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which treats SVG as an image elsewhere in Discourse. OptimizedImage.downsize is a raster ImageMagick resize and cannot meaningfully or safely reduce an SVG file in place. Large SVG uploads will repeatedly fail downsizing or may be corrupted before upload; vector formats should be excluded or handled separately.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize method definition breaks the previous four-argument API
findings.body: Ruby keeps only the last definition of self.downsize, so the new three-argument method at line 149 silently replaces the four-argument version at line 145. Existing callers using downsize(from, to, width, height) will now have height interpreted as opts, or will raise ArgumentError if an options hash is also supplied. This is an API break and can cause TypeErrors or invalid resize dimensions.

findings.title: No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior
findings.body: There are no tests for the new server-side downsizing loop, including oversized images, failed conversions, animated GIFs, SVGs, or interaction with configured size limits. These cases are likely to regress and are risky areas of this change.
